sections.title: 英语知识运用
sections.directions: Directions: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)

questions.analysis: thought 【线索】give thought to 是固定搭配 线索就在本句本身：they also need to give serious __(1)__ to how they can best。give __ to sth 表示\"认真考虑某事\"时，习惯用 give thought to / give consideration to； give idea/opinion/advice to 在英语里并不是这种\"考虑\"含义的固定搭配。 【选项】 A) thought ✓ give thought to=认真考虑，框架与语义双契合 thought 与 give __ to 构成固定搭配 give thought to sth，意思正是\"思考、考虑\"，与前面 serious 一起就是\"认真考虑\"，正好接 how they can best __(2)__ such changes 这一思考对 B) idea ✗ give idea to 不成搭配 idea 译成\"想法\"看似通顺，但英语里没有 give serious idea to 这个搭配；表达\"有想法\"用 have an idea about，不进入 give __ to 的框架。 C) opinion ✗ opinion 偏\"发表观点\"，与\"考虑\"语义错位 opinion 指\"观点、意见\"，常用搭配是 give an opinion on/about\"对…发表意见\"，主语是教 D) advice ✗ advice 是给别人的建议，主语错位 advice 指\"建议\"，固定搭配是 give advice to sb，对象是\"人\"，而本句空后接的是 to how they can best __(2)__ such changes 这样的\"事\"，且主语是教师自己在思考，不是在对外 【验证】代回原句：they also need to give serious __(1)__ to how they can best __(2)__ such need to be aware of … changes 的主旨，符合 P1 提原则的脉络。

accommodate 【线索】开篇定调=回应、适应青少年的变化 线索回到首句 Teachers need to be aware of the emotional, intellectual, and physical changes that young adults experience——教师的姿态是\"察觉并回应\"这些既成的变 【选项】A) strengthen ✗ \"加强变化\"与原意相反 strengthen 是\"加强、强化\"，与 changes 搭配会理解成\"加大青少年的身心动荡\"，与教师\"察 B) accommodate ✓ accommodate=适应/迁就，正合教师回应变化之意 accommodate 在此意为\"适应、迁就、为…作出安排\"，accommodate the changes 即\"针 对这些变化作出相应的安排\"，与首句 be aware of …changes 一脉相承，也呼应下文\"设计多 C) stimulate ✗ \"刺激变化\"方向反，且对象错配 stimulate 是\"刺激、激励\"，对象通常是人或兴趣，对 changes 用 stimulate 会理解成\"再去刺 D) enhance ✗ enhance 偏褒义\"提升质量\"，与中性的 changes 不搭 quality/effect/image；用于 changes 既色彩不合，也不是教师该做的事。 【验证】代回：how they can best __(2)__ such changes = how they can best accommodate

exercise 【线索】but not just in ways that emphasize competition 锁定\"运动\" 线索是紧跟其后的 but not just in ways that emphasize competition——只有\"运动/锻 炼\"才存在\"强调竞争与否\"的方式问题；care/nutrition/leisure 都不天然与 competition 【选项】A) care ✗ care 太宽泛，且与 competition 无关 B) nutrition ✗ 营养与竞争无关 nutrition\"营养\"虽是\"成长中的身体\"所需，但与下半句 competition 完全接不上：没有\"以竞 C) exercise ✓ exercise 与 movement 同范畴，且对 competition 敏感 \"，无缝承接 but not just in ways that emphasize competition。 D) leisure ✗ leisure 是状态，不是身体所需的活动 competition 也对不上文意。 【验证】代回：Growing bodies need movement and __(3)__, but not just in ways that emphasize competition=\"成长中的身体需要运动和锻炼，但不只是以强调竞争的方式

Because 【线索】正在适应巨大变化→所以格外敏感，是因果 前半句 they are adjusting to their new bodies and a whole host of new intellectual and emotional challenges\"他们正在适应新身体与各种新挑战\"，后半句 teenagers are especially self-conscious\"青少年格外敏感、需要被认可\"——前句是后句的原因，这是 【选项】A) If ✗ If=假设，但前半句是事实 B) Although ✗ 无让步关系，前后并不对立 C) Whereas ✗ Whereas=对比，但两句不是对照关系 D) Because ✓ Because=直接的因果 __(5)__ that comes from achieving success，因果链条紧实。 【验证】代回：\"Because they are adjusting to …, teenagers are especially self-conscious and Teachers need to be aware of … changes 的主线。

confidence 【线索】来自成功与被认可的，是\"自信\" 线索是 that comes from achieving success and knowing that their accomplishments are __(6)__ by others——\"取得成功、被他人认可\"带来的心理收益，对应的就是 self- confidence/confidence\"自信\"。其他三项（援助/指导/容忍）的来源都不是\"自己的成就 被认可\"。 【选项】A) assistance ✗ assistance 来自他人帮助，不来自自己成功 assistance\"援助\"通常 comes from sb else 而非 from achieving success；与 achieving success 不构成因果链。 B) guidance ✗ guidance 是\"指导\"，与成功的逻辑也不对 guidance 同样 comes from teachers/elders，不是 from achieving success；学生先有 guidance 才可能成功，顺序颠倒。 C) confidence ✓ confidence 直接源自成功与被认可 confidence\"自信\"正是 from achieving success and knowing that their accomplishments are admired by others 这一过程的心理产物；也接续 self-conscious 的语境——越是敏感，越 D) tolerance ✗ tolerance 与 success/认可无逻辑关系 【验证】代回：need the __(5)__ that comes from achieving success = need the confidence that comes from achieving success\"需要那种由成功获得的自信\"，承接前文 self- conscious，并为下文 more winners than losers 的设计提供心理依据。

admired 【线索】与 confidence、achieving success 同向，需褒义动词 前半句 the __(5)__ that comes from achieving success and knowing that their accomplishments are __(6)__ by others 把 confidence 与\"成就被他人 admire\"并列为 【选项】A) claimed ✗ claim 是\"声称/索取\"，主语错位 B) admired ✓ admired=被赞赏，褒义且与 confidence 同向 C) ignored ✗ ignored=被忽视，色彩反义 ignored\"被无视\"是负面体验，恰恰会摧毁 confidence，与作者主张相反。 D) surpassed ✗ surpassed=被超越，色彩反义 surpassed\"被超过\"意味着\"别人比他做得更好\"，是打击自信的体验，与 confidence comes from … 的链条相反。 【验证】代回：their accomplishments are __(6)__ by others = their accomplishments are admired by others\"他们的成就被他人赞赏\"，与 confidence 的来源完全一致，下面 more winners than losers 才能顺利展开。

wise 【线索】前文用 However 已表对竞争过多的不满 本句以 However, the typical teenage lifestyle is already filled with so much 【选项】A) improper ✗ improper=不恰当，方向反 improper\"不当的\"是负面评价，作者却是在推荐 more winners than losers，色彩相反。 B) risky ✗ risky=有风险，仍是负向 risky\"有风险的\"也是负面评价，与作者明确推荐 multiple opportunities 的态度矛盾。 C) fair ✗ fair=公平，与\"多赢少输\"矛盾 D) wise ✓ wise=明智，正合作者推荐态度 wise\"明智的\"是褒义评价，与 However 之后作者\"少竞争、多成就\"的立场一致；it would be wise to plan… 即\"明智的做法是去策划…\"。 【验证】代回：it would be __(7)__ to plan activities in which there are more winners than for example 的三个例子。

for example 【线索】后文三件事是\"多赢活动\"的具体示例 空后并列着 publishing newsletters with many student-written book reviews, __(9)__ student artwork, and sponsoring book discussion clubs 三件具体活动；它们正是前文 activities in which there are more winners than losers 的实例。这正是\"举例\"关系。 【选项】A) in effect ✗ in effect=实际上，是对前句的实质判断 B) as a result ✗ as a result=结果，但后文不是结果 \"结果\"。 C) for example ✓ for example 正好引出三个并列示例 for example\"例如\"完美对应后面 publishing/__/sponsoring 三个并列动名词——它们就是 D) in a sense ✗ in a sense=在某种意义上，方向不对 【验证】代回：\"…activities in which there are more winners than losers, for example, publishing newsletters …, displaying student artwork, and sponsoring book discussion clubs.\" 三个并列动名词正是\"举例\"，与 for example 完美咬合。

displaying 【线索】同侪是\"发表书评\"\"赞助读书会\"，目的都是让学生作品被看见 左右两件活动 publishing newsletters with many student-written book reviews 与 sponsoring book discussion clubs 都是\"让更多学生的作品/声音被看到、被参与\"，故 对 student artwork 也应是\"让它被看到\"——展示。 【选项】 A) displaying ✓ displaying student artwork=展示学生作品，与同侪同向 就被他人看到、感受 their accomplishments are __(6)__ by others 的认可。 B) describing ✗ describing=描述，不是活动 describing\"描述\"是言语行为，displaying 才是\"举办活动\"。\"描述学生作品\"在中文里像活 C) creating ✗ creating 主语错位 D) exchanging ✗ exchanging=交换，与认可成就的目的不符 exchanging\"交换\"是私下作品互换，并不能让 their accomplishments are admired by others 【验证】代回：\"publishing newsletters…, displaying student artwork, and sponsoring book discussion clubs\"，三件事都是\"让学生成就被看见\"，与 more winners than losers 完

multiple 【线索】A variety of small clubs 已暗示\"多样\"是好事 本句主语就是 A variety of small clubs\"多样的小俱乐部\"，这是作者的推荐做法；与之对 应的 opportunities 应是中性褒义\"多种多样的\"，而非\"过多的\"\"多余的\"。 【选项】A) durable ✗ durable=耐用，与 opportunities 不搭 durable\"耐用的\"用于实物（durable goods/material），不修饰抽象的 opportunities。 B) excessive ✗ excessive=过度的，贬义 C) surplus ✗ surplus=剩余的，色彩偏负面 surplus\"过剩的、多余的\"也带\"超出需求\"的意味，并非\"种类多\"。 D) multiple ✓ multiple=多种多样的，褒义中性 multiple\"多种多样的\"与 a variety of 同向，强调\"机会种类丰富\"，正合作者用小俱乐部提供 【验证】代回：A variety of small clubs can provide __(10)__ opportunities for leadership=\"多

group 【线索】上下文的 small clubs/leadership 已圈定\"团队\"语境 线索是同句 A variety of small clubs can provide __(10)__ opportunities for group dynamics。 【选项】 A) group ✓ group dynamics 是地道复合术语 group 与 dynamics 构成 group dynamics\"团体动力学/小组互动\"，正是俱乐部、读书会一类 B) individual ✗ individual dynamics 不是固定搭配，且与\"俱乐部\"矛盾 individual\"个人的\"与 dynamics 不构成固定术语，且 clubs/leadership 强调多人协作， individual 与之相反。 C) personnel ✗ personnel 是公司人事，场域错位 personnel\"人事\"是商务/公司语境用词，俱乐部场景不会用 personnel dynamics 这种说法。 D) corporation ✗ corporation 是公司，场景同样错位 【验证】代回：practice in successful __(11)__ dynamics= practice in successful group dynamics\"练习成功的团体互动\"，与 A variety of small clubs、leadership 浑然一体。

security 【线索】shy students 与 supportive adult 双线索 线索一是主语 many shy students\"害羞的学生\"——他们最需要的是\"安全感\"；线索二 是后续的 a supportive adult __(13)__ visible in the background\"在背景里若隐若现支持 的成人\"——\"支持\"的功能就是提供安全感，故空填 security。 【选项】A) consent ✗ consent=同意/许可，与心理需要无关 consent\"同意\"通常指 parental consent\"父母同意\"，与 shy students 的心理需要并非同一 B) insurance ✗ insurance=保险，物质层面 C) admission ✗ admission=入场资格，对害羞者无关键作用 D) security ✓ security=安全感，正合 shy + supportive 双线索 security\"安全感\"既贴合 shy students 的心理需要，也贴合 a supportive adult 所能提供的 【验证】代回：\"many shy students need the security of some kind of organization with a supportive adult __(13)__ visible in the background\"=\"害羞的学生需要有支持型成人

barely 【线索】in the background=不显眼，barely=几乎不 表示\"几乎不、勉强\"的程度副词 barely。\"特别可见\"\"绝对可见\"与\"背景里\"矛盾， 【选项】A) particularly ✗ particularly=特别地，与背景里矛盾 particularly\"特别明显\"把成人推向显眼位置，与\"在背景里\"相反。 B) barely ✓ barely visible=几乎看不见，正合在背景里 barely\"几乎不\"+ visible=\"勉强可见\"，正是\"成人若隐若现地支持\"的姿态，给害羞学生留 出 security 又不让其感到被监视。 C) definitely ✗ definitely=绝对地，过度显眼 definitely\"绝对/确定\"+ visible 强调\"明明白白可见\"，与背景里相反。 D) rarely ✗ rarely 是频率副词，搭配错位 rarely\"很少\"是频率，描述\"频次少\"而非\"程度低\"；rarely visible 在英语里不自然，且暗含 \"成人经常不在\"，与\"提供 security\"矛盾。 【验证】代回：\"a supportive adult barely visible in the background\"=\"一位在背景中若隐若 现的支持型成人\"，与 security、shy students 一脉相承，意境完整。

short 【线索】下文要求活动多样、可随时切换→注意力短 线索是紧接其后的 A variety of activities should be organized __(15)__ participants can remain active as long as they want and then go on to __(16)__ else without feeling 反推 attention spans 必须是 short。 【选项】A) similar ✗ similar=相似的，无对比对象 B) long ✗ long 与\"可切换\"对策矛盾 C) different ✗ different 仅指差异，未给方向 D) short ✓ short attention spans 直接驱动后文对策 【验证】代回：the young teens have __(14)__ attention spans=have short attention spans， 与下文 A variety of activities should be organized so that… 形成\"问题→对策\"链。

so that 【线索】组织活动是为了让参与者灵活进出 线索来自主从句的关系：主句 A variety of activities should be organized 是手段，从句 participants can remain active as long as they want and then go on to __(16)__ else 【选项】A) if only ✗ if only=但愿/只要，引导愿望 B) now that ✗ now that=既然，需要既成事实 C) so that ✓ so that 引导目的从句，精准对应 short attention spans 的对策。 D) even if ✗ even if=即使，让步关系，方向错 【验证】代回：\"A variety of activities should be organized so that participants can remain active as long as they want…\"=\"应组织多样活动，以便参与者想活跃多久就活跃多久

something 【线索】短注意力→换一件别的事做 线索来自全句逻辑 remain active as long as they want and then go on to __(16)__ else without feeling guilty——做完一件，再去做\"某件别的\"事，自然是 something else。 【选项】A) everything ✗ everything=一切事，过度 everything else 意思是\"所有别的事\"，与\"换一件做\"矛盾。 B) anything ✗ anything 在此显太随机 anything else 在肯定句里偏\"任何/随便什么\"，过于开放，且语气不如 something 自然。 C) nothing ✗ nothing=什么都不，与对策相反 D) something ✓ something else=某件别的事，最贴合 something else\"别的某件事\"是最自然的搭配，承接\"做了 X，再去做 Y\" 的灵活切换语境。 【验证】代回：\"…and then go on to something else without feeling guilty…\"=\"然后去做别 的事而不感到内疚\"，对策语义顺，且 without feeling guilty 也正契合\"换件事\"的轻松

down 【线索】让别人失望=let sb down 线索来自主语动作 participants can remain active as long as they want and then go on to __(16)__ else——可以自由切换却又\"不让其他参与者失望\"，正是 let sb down\"使… 【选项】A) off ✗ let off=放过/释放，语义不合 off 与 let 组合是 let sb off\"放过某人/免于惩罚\"，与\"避免让别人失望\"无关。 B) down ✓ let down=使失望，搭配与语义齐合 down 与 let 组成 let sb down\"使某人失望\"，正合\"不能让其他参与者失望\"的本意。 C) out ✗ let out=放出/泄露，语义错 D) alone ✗ let alone=更不用说，是连词性短语 alone 与 let 组成 let alone 是\"更不用说\"，固定用于负向并列，跟本句结构完全不符。 【验证】代回：\"…without letting the other participants down…\"=\"也不会让其他参与者失望 \"，与前面 without feeling guilty 一起承担\"自由切换但不失礼\"的双重保障。

On the contrary 【线索】前句否定→后句给出相反主张 前句 This does not mean that adults must accept irresponsibility\"这并不意味着成人 必须接受不负责任\"已经否定一种误解；后句 they can help students acquire a sense of commitment\"反而能帮助学生培养责任感\"立的是相反主张。这就是 on the contrary\"恰恰相反\"的标志结构。 【选项】 A) On the contrary ✓ On the contrary=恰恰相反，正合\"否X→立Y\"结构 B) On the average ✗ On the average=平均而言，统计语境 C) On the whole ✗ On the whole=总体而言，归纳口吻 On the whole\"总的来说\"用来概括，不引出立场反转。 D) On the other hand ✗ On the other hand=另一方面，需要二维对比 On the other hand 通常配 On the one hand 使用，引出对照另一面，而非\"恰恰相反\"的正面 【验证】代回：\"This does not mean that adults must accept irresponsibility. On the contrary, they can help students acquire a sense of commitment…\"=\"这并不意味着成人必须

planning 【线索】为学生\"规划/筹划\"力所能及的角色 线索来自上下文 they can help students acquire a sense of commitment by __(19)__ for roles that are within their __(20)__ and their attention spans——成人帮助学生承担 【选项】A) making ✗ make for=朝…走/导致，语义偏 making 与 for 组成 make for 是\"走向/导致\"，与\"为角色作安排\"语义对不上。 B) standing ✗ stand for=代表/支持，对象错 standing 与 for 组成 stand for 是\"代表、支持\"，对象通常是抽象理念，不接\"角色\"。 C) planning ✓ plan for=为…作规划，正合教育语境 D) taking ✗ take for=误认为，语义错 taking 与 for 组成 take for 多半是\"把…误认作\"（take A for B），不是\"为角色筹划\"。 【验证】代回：\"they can help students acquire a sense of commitment by planning for roles that are within their __(20)__ and their attention spans\"=\"通过为他们能力与注意力范

capability 【线索】与 attention spans 并列，表\"能力范围\" 线索是并列项 and their attention spans\"注意力范围\"——attention spans 是青少年的 项要么程度过高（proficiency=熟练程度），要么对象错（responsibility=责任，本就是要 培养的，不能成为\"边界\"），要么场景错（efficiency=效率）。 【选项】 A) capability ✓ capability=能力范围，与 attention spans 同类 capability\"能力\"指可承担事务的个人容量，within their capability\"在他们能力范围内\"，与 色\"。 B) responsibility ✗ responsibility 是目的，不是边界 responsibility\"责任\"在前文 a sense of commitment 里正是要培养的目标，不能反过来当\"角 C) proficiency ✗ proficiency 程度过高，对青少年不合 D) efficiency ✗ efficiency 是效率，与 attention spans 不同质 efficiency\"效率\"指做事单位投入产出，不构成\"个人容量边界\"，且 within their efficiency 不 【验证】代回：\"…roles that are within their capability and their attention spans, and by having clearly stated rules\"=\"力所能及、注意力可坚持的角色\"，与全文\"按青少年特 OVERVIEW · 通读建境 全文站在教师/组织者的视角，谈如何回应青少年的身心特点：Teachers need to be aware of the emotional, intellectual, and physical changes that young adults experience 定下主 语和话题，随后顺势提出活动设计应该多设赢家、少设输家——it would be __(7)__ to plan activities in which there are more winners than losers，并在 P2 进一步给出在自由参与与 P1 段是\"提出原则\"：青少年正在经历多重变化，需要 the __(5)__ that comes from achieving success 这种被认可感，因此活动要 more winners than losers，并用 publishing newsletters、student artwork、book discussion clubs 一串平行示例做支撑；段末把镜头 收到害羞学生身上，引出 a supportive adult __(13)__ visible in the background 这个\"成人 若隐若现\"的姿态。P2 段是\"落地与边界\"：先承认青少年 __(14)__ attention spans，所以 活动安排要让他们能自由进出；再用 This does not mean that adults must accept irresponsibility 一转，强调成人还要培养 a sense of commitment。整篇行文几乎不出现强 SENTENCE INSIGHTS ·...

sections.title: 阅读理解
sections.directions: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)

blocks.content: Wild Bill Donovan would have loved the Internet. The American spymaster who built the Office of Strategic Services in the World War Ⅱ and later laid the roots for the CIA was fascinated with information. Donovan believed in using whatever tools came to hand in the "great game" of espionage—spying as a "profession." These days the Net, which has already re-made such everyday pastimes as buying books and sending mail, is reshaping Donovan's vocation as well. The latest revolution isn't simply a matter of gentlemen reading other gentlemen's e-mail. That kind of electronic spying has been going on for decades. In the past three or four years, the World Wide Web has given birth to a whole industry of point-and-click spying. The spooks call it "open source intelligence," and as the Net grows, it is becoming increasingly influential. In 1995 the CIA held a contest to see who could compile the most data about Burundi. The winner, by a large margin, was a tiny Virginia company called Open Source Solutions, whose clear advantage was its mastery of the electronic world. Among the firms making the biggest splash in the new world is Straitford, Inc., a private intelligence- analysis firm based in Austin, Texas. Straitford makes money by selling the results of spying (covering nations from Chile to Russia) to corporations like energy-services firm McDermott International. Many of its predictions are available online at www.straitford.com. Straitford president George Friedman says he sees the online world as a kind of mutually reinforcing tool for both information collection and distribution, a spymaster's dream. Last week his firm was busy vacuuming up data bits from the far corners of the world and predicting a crisis in Ukraine. "As soon as that report runs, we'll suddenly get 500 new internet sign-ups from Ukraine," says Friedman, a former political science professor. "And we'll hear back from some of them." Open-source spying does have its risks, of course, since it can be difficult to tell good information from bad. That's where Straitford earns its keep. Friedman relies on a lean staff of 20 in Austin. Several of his staff members have military-intelligence backgrounds. He sees the firm's outsider status as the key to its success. Straitford's briefs don't sound like the usual Washington back-and-forthing, whereby agencies avoid dramatic declarations on the chance they might be wrong. Straitford, says Friedman, takes pride in its independent voice.

To paraphrase 18th-century statesman Edmund Burke, "all that is needed for the triumph of a misguided cause is that good people do nothing." One such cause now seeks to end biomedical research because of the theory that animals have rights ruling out their use in research. Scientists need to respond forcefully to animal rights advocates, whose arguments are confusing the public and thereby threatening advances in health knowledge and care. Leaders of the animal rights movement target biomedical research because it depends on public funding, and few people understand the process of health care research. Hearing allegations of cruelty to animals in research settings, many are perplexed that anyone would deliberately harm an animal. For example, a grandmotherly woman staffing an animal rights booth at a recent street fair was distributing a brochure that encouraged readers not to use anything that comes from or is tested in animals—no meat, no fur, no medicines. Asked if she opposed immunizations, she wanted to know if vaccines come from animal research. When assured that they do, she replied, "Then I would have to say yes." Asked what will happen when epidemics return, she said, "Don't worry, scientists will find some way of using computers." Such well-meaning people just don't understand. Scientists must communicate their message to the public in a compassionate, understandable way—in human terms, not in the language of molecular biology. We need to make clear the connection between animal research and a grandmother's hip replacement, a father's bypass operation, a baby's vaccinations, and even a pet's shots. To those who are unaware that animal research was needed to produce these treatments, as well as new treatments and vaccines, animal research seems wasteful at best and cruel at worst. Much can be done. Scientists could "adopt" middle school classes and present their own research. They should be quick to respond to letters to the editor, lest animal rights misinformation go unchallenged and acquire a deceptive appearance of truth. Research institutions could be opened to tours, to show that laboratory animals receive humane care. Finally, because the ultimate stakeholders are patients, the health research community should actively recruit to its cause not only well-known personalities such as Stephen Cooper, who has made courageous statements about the value of animal research, but all who receive medical treatment. If good people do nothing, there is a real possibility that an uninformed citizenry will extinguish the precious embers of medical progress.

In recent years, railroads have been combining with each other, merging into supersystems, causing heightened concerns about monopoly. As recently as 1995, the top four railroads accounted for under 70 percent of the total ton-miles moved by rails. Next year, after a series of mergers is completed, just four railroads will control well over 90 percent of all the freight moved by major rail carriers. Supporters of the new supersystems argue that these mergers will allow for substantial cost reductions and better coordinated service. Any threat of monopoly, they argue, is removed by fierce competition from trucks. But many shippers complain that for heavy bulk commodities traveling long distances, such as coal, chemicals, and grain, trucking is too costly and the railroads therefore have them by the throat. The vast consolidation within the rail industry means that most shippers are served by only one rail company. Railroads typically charge such "captive" shippers 20 to 30 percent more than they do when another railroad is competing for the business. Shippers who feel they are being overcharged have the right to appeal to the federal government's Surface Transportation Board for rate relief, but the process is expensive, time consuming, and will work only in truly extreme cases. Railroads justify rate discrimination against captive shippers on the grounds that in the long run it reduces everyone's cost. If railroads charged all customers the same average rate, they argue, shippers who have the option of switching to trucks or other forms of transportation would do so, leaving remaining customers to shoulder the cost of keeping up the line. It's a theory to which many economists subscribe, but in practice it often leaves railroads in the position of determining which companies will flourish and which will fail. "Do we really want railroads to be the arbiters of who wins and who loses in the marketplace?" asks Martin Bercovici, a Washington lawyer who frequently represents shippers. Many captive shippers also worry they will soon be hit with a round of huge rate increases. The railroad industry as a whole, despite its brightening fortunes, still does not earn enough to cover the cost of the capital it must invest to keep up with its surging traffic. Yet railroads continue to borrow billions to acquire one another, with Wall Street cheering them on. Consider the $10.2 billion bid by Norfolk Southern and CSX to acquire Conrail this year. Conrail's net railway operating income in 1996 was just $427 million, less than half of the carrying costs of the transaction. Who's going to pay for the rest of the bill? Many captive shippers fear that they will, as Norfolk Southern and CSX increase their grip on the market.

It is said that in England death is pressing, in Canada inevitable and in California optional. Small wonder. Americans' life expectancy has nearly doubled over the past century. Failing hips can be replaced, clinical depression controlled, cataracts removed in a 30-minute surgical procedure. Such advances offer the aging population a quality of life that was unimaginable when I entered medicine 50 years ago. But not even a great health-care system can cure death—and our failure to confront that reality now threatens this greatness of ours. Death is normal; we are genetically programmed to disintegrate and perish, even under ideal conditions. We all understand that at some level, yet as medical consumers we treat death as a problem to be solved. Shielded by third-party payers from the cost of our care, we demand everything that can possibly be done for us, even if it's useless. The most obvious example is late-stage cancer care. Physicians—frustrated by their inability to cure the disease and fearing loss of hope in the patient—too often offer aggressive treatment far beyond what is scientifically justified. In 1950, the US spent $12.7 billion on health care. In 2002, the cost will be $1,540 billion. Anyone can see this trend is unsustainable. Yet few seem willing to try to reverse it. Some scholars conclude that a government with finite resources should simply stop paying for medical care that sustains life beyond a certain age—say 83 or so. Former Colorado governor Richard Lamm has been quoted as saying that the old and infirm "have a duty to die and get out of the way", so that younger, healthier people can realize their potential. I would not go that far. Energetic people now routinely work through their 60s and beyond, and remain dazzlingly productive. At 78, Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone jokingly claims to be 53. Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O'Connor is in her 70s, and former surgeon general C. Everett Koop chairs an Internet start- up in his 80s. These leaders are living proof that prevention works and that we can manage the health problems that come naturally with age. As a mere 68-year-old, I wish to age as productively as they have. Yet there are limits to what a society can spend in this pursuit. As a physician, I know the most costly and dramatic measures may be ineffective and painful. I also know that people in Japan and Sweden, countries that spend far less on medical care, have achieved longer, healthier lives than we have. As a nation, we may be overfunding the quest for unlikely cures while underfunding research on humbler therapies that could improve people's lives.

questions.analysis: 【判型】Q21 是一个待补全的陈述句 The emergence of the Net has____.，问"互联网出现之后发 生了什么客观结果"，无 infer/suggest/imply 等推断标志，也不问主旨或态度。 【拆句】The emergence of the Net has____. 是一个简单的现在完成时陈述句，主语为 The emergence of the Net，谓语 has 后面留空待补——空格里要填的是过去分词短语（动作 【定位】P1 These days the Net, which has already re-made such everyday pastimes as buying books and sending mail, is reshaping Donovan's vocation as well. 报业）。 【选项】A) 与原文相反 选项 received support from fans like Donovan 把因果颠倒——原文是"Donovan 若 还在世会喜欢互联网"（虚拟语气 would have loved），并不是"Donovan 真的支持了 互联网"；Donovan 早已不在世，更谈不上 received support。 B) ✓ 正确 is reshaping Donovan's vocation ↔ remolded the intelligence services （reshape）+ intelligence services（Donovan's vocation），无引申、无偏移，直接 锁定 B。 选项 restored many common pastimes 把 has already re-made such everyday pastimes as buying books and sending mail 的 re-made（重塑、改变形式）偷换成 选项 revived spying as a profession 中的 revive（使复活、复兴）暗示"间谍业曾衰 decades；这是无中生有的引申。

questions.question: The text intends to express the idea that____. Part B Directions: Read the following text carefully and then translate the underlined segments into Chinese. Write your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. ( 10 points) Human beings in all times and places think about their world and wonder at their place in it. Humans are thoughtful and creative, possessed of insatiable curiosity. (41)Furthermore, humans have the ability to modify the environment in which they live, thus subjecting all other life forms to their own peculiar ideas and fancies. Therefore, it is important to study humans in all their richness and diversity in a calm and systematic manner, with the hope that the knowledge resulting from such studies can lead humans to a more harmonious way of living with themselves and with all other life forms on this planet Earth. "Anthropology" derives from the Greek words anthropos "human" and logos "the study of." By its very name, anthropology encompasses the study of all humankind. Anthropology is one of the social sciences. (42)Social science is that branch of intellectual enquiry which seeks to study humans and their endeavors in the same reasoned, orderly, systematic, and dispassioned manner that natural scientists use for the study of natural phenomena. Social science disciplines include geography, economics, political science, psychology, and sociology. Each of these social sciences has a subfield or specialization which lies particularly close to anthropology. All the social sciences focus upon the study of humanity. Anthropology is a field-study oriented discipline which makes extensive use of the comparative method in analysis. (43)The emphasis on data gathered first-hand, combined with a cross-cultural perspective brought to the analysis of cultures past and present, makes this study a unique and distinctly important social science. Anthropological analyses rest heavily upon the concept of culture. Sir Edward Tylor's formulation of the concept of culture was one of the great intellectual achievements of 19th century science. (44)Tylor defined culture as "…that complex whole which includes belief, art, morals, law, custom, and any other capabilities and habits acquired by man as a member of society." This insight, so profound in its simplicity, opened up an entirely new way of perceiving and understanding human life. Implicit within Tylor's definition is the concept that culture is learned, shared, and patterned behavior. (45)Thus, the anthropological concept of "culture," like the concept of "set" in mathematics, is an abstract concept which makes possible immense amounts of concrete research and understanding.
